edges.description: Atlas routes to its own human-readable navigation contract so route semantics can be checked before destination content is interpreted.
Atlas source policy defines owner-local truth, freshness, and open-world constraints for navigation metadata.
Atlas implementation status prevents a merged route contract from being mistaken for UI consumption, runtime routing, synchronization, or production authority.
The research evidence directory expands research questions into exact evidence, current interpretation, and long-form history without becoming research truth itself.
The directory provides the detailed Atlas route for Graphiti Fractal retrieval relevance while exact laboratory artifacts remain authoritative for run-specific evidence.
FM-16 claims should pass through the reconciled experiment/evidence route rather than treating the Atlas narrative as a frozen run output.
Atlas and Knowledge Tree share navigation-only/open-world discipline; neither gains destination authority from a route or pointer.
The Tree's own authority model is the primary guardrail against treating navigation metadata as evidence, Canon, truth, or permission.
The update protocol defines owning-source-first maintenance and when changed relations belong in Crosswalk or Atlas instead of the Tree.
When a substantive cross-project relationship changes, the update protocol routes that semantic change to Crosswalk rather than making the Tree its owner.
When global navigation changes, the Tree update protocol routes the navigation-layer change to Atlas.
The versioned contract can be implemented as documentation/data while UI/runtime consumption remains separately unimplemented and unauthorized.
Source policy constrains how the navigation contract may interpret freshness, ownership, absent routes, and destination authority.
